subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 22-year-old woman with celiac disease has several recurrent, painful, shallow round ulcers on the buccal mucosa. Each lesion has a yellowish exudate and heals over about a week, only to recur months later.
question: Which condition best explains these oral lesions?

options.text: Oral squamous cell carcinoma
Pleomorphic adenoma
Sialolithiasis
Warthin tumor
Recurrent aphthous stomatitis

explanation_correct: Aphthous ulcers, or canker sores, are common painful, shallow, round to oval oral ulcers covered by a yellowish exudate. Recurrent aphthous stomatitis is associated with celiac disease, inflammatory bowel disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, Behçet syndrome, and HIV infection. The recurrent painful shallow ulcers in this patient with celiac disease are classic.

explanation_incorrect.A: Oral squamous cell carcinoma presents as a nonhealing ulcer with irregular margins and raised borders, not recurring shallow ulcers that heal.
explanation_incorrect.B: Pleomorphic adenoma is a painless salivary gland mass with chondromyxoid stroma, not an ulcerated oral mucosal lesion.
explanation_incorrect.C: Sialolithiasis causes preprandial or periprandial pain and swelling of a major salivary gland, not shallow oral ulcers.
explanation_incorrect.D: Warthin tumor is a benign cystic parotid tumor seen in smokers, not a recurrent painful ulcer.

educationalObjective: Aphthous ulcers are painful shallow oral ulcers with yellow exudate and recur in celiac disease, IBD, SLE, Behçet syndrome, and HIV.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 58-year-old man who smokes and drinks heavily has a nonhealing ulcer on the lateral tongue with irregular margins and raised borders. Examination also shows a white patch on the floor of his mouth that has been present for months.
question: Which diagnosis is most likely, and what does the white patch represent?

options.text: Aphthous ulcer; the white patch is a Warthin tumor
Mucoepidermoid carcinoma; the white patch is erythroplakia
Sialadenitis; the white patch is a canker sore
Squamous cell carcinoma; the white patch is leukoplakia, a precursor lesion
Pleomorphic adenoma; the white patch is an aphthous ulcer

explanation_correct: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common malignancy of the oral cavity and usually affects the tongue. It is associated with tobacco, alcohol, and HPV-16, and presents as a nonhealing ulcer with irregular margins and raised borders. Leukoplakia is a white patch and erythroplakia a red patch; both are precursor lesions of oral squamous cell carcinoma.

explanation_incorrect.A: Aphthous ulcers are shallow, painful, and self-limited rather than nonhealing with raised borders; Warthin tumor is a parotid lesion in smokers.
explanation_incorrect.B: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is a salivary gland tumor with mucinous and squamous components; erythroplakia is red, not white.
explanation_incorrect.C: Sialadenitis is inflammation of a salivary gland; a canker sore is an aphthous ulcer and not a persistent white patch.
explanation_incorrect.E: Pleomorphic adenoma is a benign parotid mass, and an aphthous ulcer is a shallow painful lesion, not a white patch.

educationalObjective: Oral squamous cell carcinoma is the most common oral malignancy and is preceded by leukoplakia or erythroplakia.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 45-year-old man has recurrent right submandibular pain and swelling that begin just before or during meals. Symptoms have recurred over several months and are worse when he is dehydrated after working outdoors.
question: Which condition best explains this presentation?

options.text: Acute sialadenitis caused by mumps virus
Pleomorphic adenoma of the parotid gland
Sialolithiasis with salivary stasis in a major duct
Oral squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue
Sjogren syndrome with autoimmune glandular destruction

explanation_correct: Sialolithiasis is stone formation in the major salivary gland ducts, including the parotid, submandibular, and sublingual ducts. It is associated with salivary stasis from dehydration and with trauma, and it presents with recurrent preprandial or periprandial pain and swelling in the affected gland. Eating stimulates salivation against an obstructed duct, producing the characteristic mealtime symptoms.

explanation_incorrect.A: Mumps causes viral sialadenitis with diffuse glandular inflammation, not recurrent meal-related obstruction from dehydration.
explanation_incorrect.B: Pleomorphic adenoma is a painless, slowly growing parotid mass rather than episodic pain and swelling with meals.
explanation_incorrect.D: Oral squamous cell carcinoma produces a nonhealing tongue ulcer and does not cause parotid or submandibular mealtime swelling.
explanation_incorrect.E: Sjogren syndrome causes immune-mediated sicca symptoms, not the recurrent ductal obstruction described here.

educationalObjective: Sialolithiasis causes recurrent pre-/periprandial salivary gland pain and swelling from stasis and duct obstruction.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 62-year-old man has a slowly growing, largely painless parotid mass. He then develops weakness of the facial nerve on that side. Histologic examination shows both mucinous and squamous components.
question: Which diagnosis is most consistent with these findings?

options.text: Pleomorphic adenoma, a benign tumor with chondromyxoid stroma that recurs if ruptured
Mucoepidermoid carcinoma, the most common malignant salivary gland tumor
Warthin tumor, a benign cystic tumor with germinal centers in smokers
Aphthous ulcer, a painful shallow lesion with a yellow exudate
Sialolithiasis, a stone in a major duct causing preprandial pain

explanation_correct: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is the most common malignant salivary gland tumor and is composed of mucinous and squamous components. Salivary gland tumors usually present as painless masses, but facial paralysis or pain suggests malignant involvement, as in this patient. This combination of histology and facial nerve weakness points to mucoepidermoid carcinoma.

explanation_incorrect.A: Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common benign salivary tumor, with chondromyxoid stroma and epithelium; it recurs if incompletely excised or ruptured but does not typically invade the facial nerve.
explanation_incorrect.C: Warthin tumor is a benign cystic lesion with germinal centers, often bilateral or multifocal, and is associated with smoking.
explanation_incorrect.D: An aphthous ulcer is a superficial painful oral mucosal lesion with yellow exudate, not a parotid mass with facial nerve involvement.
explanation_incorrect.E: Sialolithiasis produces intermittent ductal pain and swelling related to meals and is not a neoplasm with mucinous and squamous histology.

educationalObjective: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is the most common malignant salivary tumor; facial nerve paralysis suggests malignancy.
source: Generated from 9. Gastrointestinal.pdf - Pathology: Oral pathologies

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 38-year-old woman has a painless, slowly enlarging parotid mass. It is excised, but the capsule is ruptured during the operation. Histology shows epithelial elements embedded in a chondromyxoid stroma.
question: Which tumor is this, and what is a recognized consequence of intraoperative rupture?

options.text: Pleomorphic adenoma; local recurrence
Warthin tumor; transformation into mucoepidermoid carcinoma
Mucoepidermoid carcinoma; development of facial paralysis
Sialadenitis caused by Staphylococcus aureus; abscess formation
Aphthous stomatitis; recurrence in association with celiac disease

explanation_correct: Pleomorphic adenoma, also called benign mixed tumor, is the most common salivary gland tumor. It is composed of chondromyxoid stroma and epithelium and recurs if it is incompletely excised or ruptured intraoperatively. It may also undergo malignant transformation. The painless parotid mass and characteristic histology in this patient are classic.

explanation_incorrect.B: Warthin tumor is a benign cystic tumor with germinal centers, often bilateral or multifocal in smokers; rupture is not its hallmark complication.
explanation_incorrect.C: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is malignant with mucinous and squamous components and lacks the chondromyxoid stroma described here.
explanation_incorrect.D: Sialadenitis is inflammation from obstruction, infection such as S aureus, or immune mechanisms, not a mass with chondromyxoid stroma.
explanation_incorrect.E: Aphthous stomatitis consists of painful shallow oral ulcers with yellow exudate, not a parotid neoplasm.

educationalObjective: Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common benign salivary tumor and recurs if incompletely excised or ruptured.
